content_preview.title: China Recovers Long March 10B Booster With Net Capture at Sea, Becoming Second Nation to Land an Orbital-Class Rocket
content_preview.summary: CASC's new Long March 10B caught its own booster in a sea-based net on its maiden flight July 10, joining SpaceX and Blue Origin as the only operators to recover an orbital-class rocket stage.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) launched the new Long March 10B rocket on its maiden flight from the Hainan Commercial Space Launch Site at 12:15 a.m. Eastern (0415 UTC) on July 10, 2026, and recovered the vehicle's first stage using a net-based capture system on a ship at sea, [according to SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/china-becomes-second-country-to-recover-orbital-booster-with-long-march-10b/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know) at 673 words, within the 400-1200 range for the category. Clear, neutral, technically precise coverage of the Long March 10B maiden flight and net-based first-stage recovery. The Overview paragraph and summary are tightly sourced to SpaceNews and Scientific American and hold up completely under verification.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots read in full from sources/2026-07/china-recovers-long-march-10b-booster-with-net-capture-at-sea-becoming-second-nation-to-land-an-orbital-class-rocket/ (sha256 of decompressed content verified against manifest.json for source-0 through source-4; all matched). source-0.html.gz (SpaceNews, Andrew Jones) confirms launch time/site, recovery mechanics, vehicle specs (63m, 760,000kg, 7x YF-100K, 890 tons thrust, 16,000kg LEO payload), undisclosed satellite payload, the Linghang Zhe recovery vessel, six-minute post-separation recovery timing, CASC's end-of-2026 reflight intent, and the Long March 10A/Mengzhou/lunar-2030 background. source-1.html.gz (Scientific American, Lee Billings) confirms the 'second organization/elite club with SpaceX and Blue Origin' framing, the CASC quote about first controlled/net-based recovery, the verbatim 'four comparatively lightweight landing hooks' quote, and the 'no flawless first-launch recovery by anyone else' claim -- but does NOT mention Mengzhou or frame the flight as a 'validation' of the Long March 10A design (see Finding 1 below; that content is SpaceNews's, not Scientific American's). source-2.html.gz (Xinhua/english.news.cn) confirms the recovery-ship dimensions (144m x 50m, 25,000 tonnes, delivered Nov. 2025 by CALT), the Chen Muye quote on net-based recovery benefits (verbatim), the Long Lehao quote on 10A/10B/10C forming the 'backbone' of China's transportation system (verbatim), and Xu Xuelei's platform-design description -- though Xinhua itself renders the Xu Xuelei material as indirect/reported speech ('said in an interview that...'), not a direct quotation (see Finding 2). source-3.html.gz (Global Times, short wire item) confirms the vertical-return/recovery sentence used in paragraph 3. source-4.html.gz (Global Times, longer feature) confirms rocket specs, the 'second country... to master vertical rocket recovery technology' framing, the end-of-2026 reused-first-stage-test timeline, and the Sun Zhenlian capture-mechanism quote -- though the article's rendering of that quote is a paraphrase, not verbatim (see Finding 1). The internal cross-link to the June 1 Long March 12B article was checked against src/content/articles/2026-06/06-china-debuts-reusable-long-march-12b-... and the June 1 date is correct.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The headline, summary, and Overview lead are fully supported by the cited sources and verified verbatim. Two recoverable issues found in the body (both flagged as corrections, see Findings): (1) a quoted line attributed to Sun Zhenlian paraphrases Global Times's actual wording, and a second passage presents Xinhua's indirect/reported speech from Xu Xuelei as if it were a direct quotation (the words match Xinhua's text exactly, but Xinhua did not put them in quotation marks); (2) a sentence about the flight 'validating' the Long March 10A design for the Mengzhou crew spacecraft is attributed to Scientific American, but that specific content (the 10A-validation framing and the Mengzhou name) appears in SpaceNews, not in the Scientific American snapshot -- the facts themselves are true and independently verifiable in SpaceNews, so this is a wrong-outlet citation rather than a fabrication. A minor, non-corrected observation: the claim that the planned Long March 10C variant will 'support satellite-constellation and crewed missions' slightly overstates Global Times, which ties satellite-constellation deployment to the 10B and crewed missions to the 10/10A family, not explicitly to 10C; this is a soft inference from the 'backbone of China's space transportation system' framing rather than an invented fact, and does not rise to a formal correction.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Attributions are consistently hedged ('according to', 'reported'), no editorializing or sensationalized language, and the 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags open questions (satellite payload details, exact reflight date) rather than speculating.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Searched src/content/articles/ for prior 'Long March' coverage: no existing article covers the Long March 10B or this recovery event. The June 1, 2026 Long March 12B debut (src/content/articles/2026-06/06-china-debuts-reusable-long-march-12b-...) is a different rocket and different event; this submission correctly cross-references it as related background rather than duplicating it. Not a duplicate of any recently published article.
concerns: A quote attributed to Sun Zhenlian ('like powerful hands firmly grasping the rocket') paraphrases Global Times's actual wording ('like a pair of powerful hands that firmly grasp the rocket'), and a passage attributed to Xu Xuelei is presented as a direct quotation though Xinhua rendered it as indirect/reported speech.

A sentence about the flight validating the Long March 10A design for the Mengzhou crew spacecraft is cited to Scientific American, but that content is drawn from SpaceNews; the underlying facts are accurate and independently verifiable, but the citation is to the wrong outlet.

One source domain, english.news.cn (Xinhua's official English portal), is not on config/source_allowlist.txt even though the sibling domain xinhuanet.com is allowlisted; this is a config gap, not a reliability concern about the outlet itself.
recommendations: File a corrections record covering the two quote/attribution issues and the outlet misattribution.
Add english.news.cn to config/source_allowlist.txt alongside xinhuanet.com so future Xinhua English-portal citations do not trip the allowlist check.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A well-sourced, accurately-led News piece with two recoverable body-level issues (a paraphrased/misformatted quote pair and one wrong-outlet citation for an otherwise true and verifiable fact). Neither issue touches the headline, summary, or lead. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS: publish with a corrections record.
